Sparse log-concave nonnegative matrix factorization

Source: R/splogconNMF.R
splogconNMF.Rd

Recover a parsimonious set of compounds from multichannel signals, with nonnegative spectra, hard log-concave elution profiles and a smooth background. Fast spectral fusion and local native updates accommodate broad, asymmetric and shark-fin peaks while retaining all original outcome channels.

Usage

splogconNMF(
  X,
  y,
  family = poisson("identity"),
  background = NULL,
  lambda = "gic",
  dispersion = NULL,
  theta = NULL,
  precluster = NULL,
  weights = NULL,
  offset = NULL,
  correlation = c("auto", "none", "lag1"),
  ncores = NULL,
  control = list(),
  start = NULL,
  verbose = FALSE
)

Arguments

X

Nonnegative scans-by-candidates matrix, typically shifted copies of a point-spread function from [convmatrix()] or [L0glm_blind_deco()]. Columns must have contiguous log-concave positive support. Dense and sparse inputs are accepted and stored sparsely; columns are normalized to unit sum.

y

Numeric scans-by-channels matrix or a single-channel vector.

family

Identity-link noise family: `gaussian`, `poisson`, `quasipoisson`, `mgcv::nb`, `Gamma`, [nb1()], [Gamma_scale()] or [Gamma_censored()]. The corresponding names, including `"nb"`, `"nb1"` and `"Gamma_scale"`, are also accepted. Count likelihoods require integer counts; quasipoisson accepts nonnegative intensities. Gaussian observations may be negative; their fitted latent signals remain nonnegative.

background

Optional nonnegative scans-by-basis matrix, for example `splines::bs(time, df=6, intercept=TRUE)`. Coefficients are nonnegative and unpenalized. `NULL` fits without a background.

lambda

`"gic"` (default), `"aic"`, `"bic"`, `"ebic"`, `"mbic"`, or a nonnegative numeric compound penalty. See Details for its scale.

dispersion

Known common Gaussian variance, quasipoisson scale, Gamma dispersion, NB1 variance-to-mean ratio or common Gamma scale. `NULL` estimates a pooled value from temporal differences and freezes it. Parameters supplied in a [signal_families] object are used when this argument is omitted. Poisson and NB2 use unit dispersion.

theta

NB2 shape, shared by all original channels. `NULL` estimates and freezes a temporal moment estimate; a positive value fixes it; a negative value initializes at its absolute value and enables pooled likelihood updates. A fixed shape in the supplied NB family is respected.

precluster

`NULL` or `FALSE` uses every channel throughout. `TRUE` uses up to 32 groups; an integer supplies another maximum. Size-adjusted Poisson clustering, aggregation, selection and fusion operate in that reduced space, followed by refinement on all original channels.

weights

Nonnegative likelihood weights: a scalar, row vector or matrix matching `y`. `NULL` uses one. Zero weights omit observations.

offset

Known nonnegative mean contribution, in the same supported formats as `weights`. `NULL` uses zero. It is included on the response scale because the link is identity.

correlation

`"auto"` or `"lag1"` estimates an optional lag-one working adjustment to the selection penalty. `"none"` uses independent observations; a number between zero and 0.49 supplies the lag-one correlation.

ncores

OpenMP workers. `NULL` uses the detected physical cores.

control

Named list: `broad_repeats=1L`, `full_sweeps=1L`, `final_polishes=1L`, `native_sweeps=6L`, `block_sweeps=6L`, `psf_width=NULL`, `screen_factor=1`, `censor=0.5`, `linkage="ward"`, `joint_trials=NULL`. The latter uses direct Poisson fusion for Poisson data and joint local refinement for the other families. `psf_width` is the typical FWHM in scans, inferred from the middle design column. `screen_factor` scales the initial selection penalty. `censor` is the Gamma detection limit: recorded zero intensities are left-censored below this value; positive values must be at least the limit. Zero requests an uncensored Gamma model. A supplied Gamma family constructor provides its own detection limit unless overridden here. `linkage` may be `"ward"` or `"bregman"`. `joint_trials` allows overlapping compounds to adjust together during local fusion refinement.

start

Optional list `H`, `S` and `alpha`, with original dimensions. `H` has scans in rows and compounds in columns; `S` has compounds in rows and all original channels in columns. `alpha` contains background coefficients and defaults to zero. Profiles are normalized with the inverse change applied to spectra. A restart bypasses initial screening and preclustering; nonnegative spectral entries can reopen during refitting.

verbose

Print stage timings, objective changes and compound counts.

object, x

A fitted `splogconNMF` object.

...

Further method arguments.

k

Complexity multiplier for [stats::AIC()].

Value

An object of class `splogconNMF`, containing sparse unit-sum profiles `H`, spectra `S`, background coefficients `alpha`, the background basis, fitted means `mu`, `rank`, resolved noise settings `spec`, original data, offsets and weights, `objective`, `loglik`, stage ledger `history`, `ledger_error`, aggregation diagnostics, controls and timings `seconds`. `coef()` returns spectra and `fitted()` the full mean matrix. `logLik()`, `AIC()`, `BIC()`, `GIC()`, `EBIC()` and `MBIC()` score the returned model.

Details

**Model and selection criterion.** With scans in rows, write $$\mu=HS+B A+O,\qquad H,S,A\geq0.$$ Each profile has unit sum, contiguous positive support and \(\Delta^2\log H_{\cdot r}\leq0\) on that support. The objective is $$J=-2\sum_{ij}w_{ij}\ell(y_{ij};\mu_{ij},\nu)+\lambda_R K,$$ where \(K\) is the number of compounds and \(\nu\) contains the shared noise parameters. An IC preset uses \(\lambda_R=m\kappa\lambda_{IC}\), with \(m\) original channels. A numeric `lambda` supplies the total compound penalty before multiplication by \(\kappa\). The initial grouped fit uses \(\lambda_R/m\). Each compound contributes one selection count; spectral entries and profile complexity have no separate penalty. This is a compound-count model-selection convention. The IC methods use \(mK\) plus the number of estimated shared noise parameters as their complexity count; it is distinct from counting every free profile ordinate.

**Initialization and local updates.** A variance-matched grouped Poisson working fit supplies candidate components, using [L0glm.fit()] with relaxed refitting and compulsory background columns. The subsequent updates use the specified family's exact score and likelihood. For a spectral coefficient or profile ordinate, the conditional mean is \(\mu_i=r_i+x_i b\), with the other components fixed in \(r_i\). If \(g_i\) and \(I_i>0\) are the negative log-likelihood score and a positive working curvature, a nonnegative quadratic proposal is $$b^+=\max\left\{0,b-\frac{\sum_i w_i x_i g_i} {\sum_i w_i x_i^2 I_i}\right\}.$$ Backtracking checks the actual loss, with an explicit zero-boundary check. Poisson and quasipoisson use a specialized bracketed scalar likelihood solve. Background terms use small constrained quadratic solves, and all channels run independently through OpenMP. Poisson profile proposals use four warm native IRLS iterations. During a full profile sweep, an adaptive ridge tether centred on the preceding profile stabilizes weak tails, with local penalty weights proportional to the inverse squared profile ordinate. The final acceptance test uses the complete likelihood-and-rank criterion.

Spectral clustering proposes fusions without fitting a model. It compares normalized spectra through Jensen–Shannon information loss and joins overlapping compatible profiles. A least concave majorant of the log profile enforces hard log concavity. Local refinement reallocates signal between overlapping compounds and checks the actual criterion. Every complete stage is accepted against its full working data, and final refinement and scoring use all original observations. `history` records each accepted or rejected stage; `ledger_error` checks the accumulated criterion change.

**Noise models.** Gaussian variance is \(\phi\); quasipoisson variance is \(\phi\mu\); NB2 variance is \(\mu+\mu^2/\theta\); standard Gamma variance is \(\phi\mu^2\). NB1 has variance \(\phi\mu\), while common-scale Gamma has shape \(\mu/b\) and scale \(b\), hence variance \(b\mu\). Their exact scores and densities are given in [signal_families]. A censored Gamma zero contributes a log CDF at the detection limit, and a positive observation contributes its log density. For quasipoisson, \(\ell_Q=\{y\log\mu-\mu-\log\Gamma(y+1)\}/\phi\); `logLik()` marks this scaled kernel with `quasi=TRUE`, and the regular IC method names return quasi-information criteria. Compare candidate ranks under the same family and frozen scale.

For an updated NB2 shape, the pooled score is $$U_\theta=\sum_{ij}w_{ij}\left\{\psi(y_{ij}+\theta)-\psi(\theta) +\log\theta+1-\log(\theta+\mu_{ij}) -\frac{y_{ij}+\theta}{\theta+\mu_{ij}}\right\}.$$ Bounded Newton proposals in \(\log\theta\) are backtracked against the pooled likelihood. One common shape is retained across original channels.

**Temporal calibration and aggregation.** [temporal_dispersion()] uses fourth and eighth differences in quieter parts of a smoothed pilot signal. This estimates the marginal noise scale; an optional lag-one working correction multiplies the rank penalty by \(\kappa=1+2\widehat\rho_1\). It leaves the fitted variance parameter on its marginal scale. This local covariance approximation is recorded in `spec`; use `correlation="none"` for independent simulated data.

Preclustering uses [glm_cluster()] with `size_fac=colSums(pmax(y,0))`, removing differences in total ion intensity when comparing channel shapes. Poisson and common-parameter NB1 latent signals add exactly; independent common-scale Gamma latent signals also add. Standard NB2 and Gamma use moment-matched aggregate parameters. Censored Gamma sums and differing channel weights give working approximations in the reduced space. The returned model always contains all original channels, their offsets and their original-channel likelihood.

See also

[GCMSdeco()], [L0glm_blind_deco()], [L0glm.fit()], [glm_cluster()]

Examples

set.seed(12)
n <- 300L
psf <- convkernel("gaussian", 21L, list(sigma = 2))
X <- convmatrix(psf, n)
H <- cbind(X[, c(45, 95, 160, 235)],
           pmax(0, 1 - abs(seq_len(n) - 185) / 22))
H <- H %*% Matrix::Diagonal(x = 1 / Matrix::colSums(H))
S <- matrix(rexp(5 * 8, rate = 1 / 3000), 5, 8)
B <- splines::bs(seq_len(n), df = 4, intercept = TRUE)
mu <- as.matrix(H %*% S) + B %*% matrix(20, 4, 8)
Y <- matrix(rpois(length(mu), mu), n, 8)
fit <- splogconNMF(X, Y, background = B, family = poisson("identity"),
  precluster = 4L, correlation = "none", ncores = 2L)
fit
c(compounds = fit$rank, GIC = GIC(fit), seconds = fit$seconds[["total"]])
matplot(fit$H, type = "l", lty = 1, xlab = "Scan", ylab = "Elution profile")

# For overdispersed intensities, estimate one common noise scale from temporal
# differences. Selection and fusion use four groups; the result has all channels.
Yq <- 5 * matrix(rpois(length(mu), mu / 5), n, 8)
fitq <- splogconNMF(X, Yq, background = B, family = quasipoisson("identity"),
  precluster = 4L, correlation = "none", ncores = 2L)
GIC(fitq)

# Other identity-link choices include gaussian(), mgcv::nb(), Gamma(),
# nb1(dispersion=5, link="identity"), and
# Gamma_scale(scale=5, link="identity", censor=0.5).
